suggested_requirements.text: The system shall accept job submission parameters including executable location, input data sets, system type, maximum run length, job type, budget, and deadline.
The system shall verify user identity upon job submission.
The system shall allow users and administrators to view the status of submitted jobs.
The system shall allow users and administrators to cancel submitted jobs.
The system shall allow users and administrators to modify specific job parameters such as output directory or deadline.
The system shall determine whether to accept or reject a job based on budget, deadline, and execution time.
The system shall calculate job priority using the Stride Scheduling algorithm based on budget and deadline.
The system shall select an execution host and queue based on job budget, execution time, and deadline.
The system shall dispatch jobs to the selected execution host and queue.
The system shall update cluster status including CPU load, node status, and queue length upon job scheduling or removal.
The system shall perform time-slicing between executing jobs using the Stride Scheduling algorithm.
The system shall provide administrative security to prevent unauthorized alteration of scheduling criteria or resource allocation.
The system shall ensure the privacy of user job status.
The system shall have a maximum job submission response time of 1 minute.
The system shall ensure all jobs are completed within a 10% error allowance of their deadlines.
The system shall ensure the maximum cost charged to the user does not exceed the user-submitted budget.
The system shall have a maximum bug rate of 1 bug per 1000 lines of code.
The system shall recover from a system outage in less than five minutes.
The system shall provide a command-line interface for users to submit jobs, query costs, monitor status, cancel jobs, and check credit/usage.
The system shall provide a command-line interface for administrators to check node status, usage history, job status, node load, and modify cost/policy/job state.
The system shall be a sub-component of the Sun Grid Engine.
The system shall be written in standard C.
The system shall use the Hungarian Naming Convention for all code.
The system shall be released under the GNU General Purpose License.
The system shall provide online documentation in the form of Linux man pages.
